proposals.reason: Apply, Apply all, Skip, permissions and fork handling are now built; the doc says acting on proposals does nothing.
proposals.content:
# Proposal output

When a runner returns proposals, the gate reports them three ways on the PR: the `pollux-agent` check run (`action_required`, listing doc paths and reasons), one review comment per proposal on the head commit, and one summary comment on the PR. A "no impact" result sets the check to `success` with the reason and posts no comments. Proposals are acted on from those comments (see [Apply and Skip](#apply-and-skip)).

## Apply and Skip

Anyone with write access can act on a proposal; the gate checks the sender's repository permission through the GitHub API before doing anything. Comments that ask for nothing cost no GitHub call. A sender without write access gets a reply and a `confused` reaction, and a refused tick is unticked again. The bot adds `eyes` when it picks an action up and swaps it for `rocket` when the action completes, or `confused` when it was refused with a reply saying why. Comments from bots are ignored.

Actions come from checkboxes or from `/pollux-agent` commands (an issue comment whose first line starts with the command):

- **Apply this change** (review comment checkbox): applies that one proposal.
- **Apply all** (summary checkbox) or `/pollux-agent apply`: applies every open proposal.
- **Skip this commit** / **Skip this PR** (summary checkboxes), `/pollux-agent skip <reason>`, or `/pollux-agent skip-pr <reason>`: concludes the check `success`, titled "Skipped by @user". A commit skip covers only the head it was made at; a PR skip covers every later head and stops proposals from being refreshed. Without a reason, the bot asks for one and the same user's next comment on the PR becomes the reason. Reasons are echoed in the summary and check, so they are cut to one line and 500 characters, and `@` mentions and checkbox markup are broken.

Apply commits all targeted proposals as one commit on the PR branch, pushed without force, replacing each section's exact original text (which must occur exactly once in the doc) and adding index entries for new docs to the `## Index` list of `docs/README.md`. It refuses, with a reply and nothing committed, when the PR is from a fork the bot cannot push to, is closed, has moved off the head the proposals were made for, has a stored proposal that no longer matches its doc, or GitHub rejects the commit (for example a protected branch). If the branch moves while applying, nothing is committed and a re-analysis follows. The intended commit is saved before the push, so a crash or a push handled before the retry still marks the proposals applied: the retry finds the commit by its saved message and parent and adopts it. Applied proposals show their comment's Apply box ticked and their commit in the summary. A redelivery only posts what is still missing.

## Failures and Re-run

Every analysis first creates an in-progress check and saves an armed run (nonce, 10-minute deadline), so a check is never missing or left pending: the deadline sweep closes any armed run neutral (see [Job queue](job-queue.md)). Any failure ends the check neutral, titled "Analysis failed" (or "PR too large to analyze"), with a one-line fixed cause that never quotes model output, provider responses, or artifact text; the detail stays in the server log. A superseded or interrupted analysis is not a failure: the next analysis closes its check as superseded.

A successful summary opens with "**pollux-agent** proposes N doc update(s)." (open proposals only) and has no Re-run box. After a failure the summary instead opens with the cause and ends with an unticked "- [ ] Re-run analysis". Proposals from an earlier successful run stay listed and are not marked outdated, because a failure says nothing about them. Ticking the box (an edited `issue_comment` on the summary comment, identified by its saved comment ID; a tick elsewhere or any other edit does nothing) or clicking GitHub's Re-run on the check (`check_run` `rerequested`) enqueues a `pull_request`-kind job. It fetches the PR's current head and starts a fresh analysis with a new check run, and the box is unticked when that analysis next writes the summary (on its result or its failure; an Actions re-run leaves it ticked until the workflow finishes). The tick still needs write access like any other action. A re-run of a closed PR, or a second one while an analysis of the same head is still running, does nothing, so repeated ticks cannot stack model runs.

A re-run waits for an analysis already running on the PR instead of cancelling it, and a push supersedes a re-run like any analysis, so only the newest head produces the final check; a same-head check it replaces reads "Superseded by a re-run". For forks, `check_run` may carry no pull request; the handler then finds the PR by the check's head SHA in stored state. Posting comments after a result is retried a few times with backoff, and a retry adopts comments already created by their markers, so nothing is duplicated.

## Where the section text comes from

Each proposal carries the current text of the section it replaces and that text's head-side line range in the doc. The server runner fills both from its own checkout of the head commit (see [Server runner](server-runner.md)); the Actions runner fills them from the doc fetched at the head SHA through the contents API (see [Actions runner](actions-runner.md)); they are never model output and are kept out of the generated JSON schema. Both are empty for a new doc. The range runs from the heading through the section's last line, including trailing blank lines. The gate may import only `internal/review`, so it cannot parse docs itself; it trusts these fields. A proposal whose doc or section is missing at the head, or whose heading matches more than one section, leaves them empty, and its comment degrades to the checkbox variant; guessing the section would let a suggestion overwrite the wrong one.

A proposal's content replaces the whole section, heading line included, because a suggestion replaces the heading line too. Both runner prompts and the generated schema say so. If the content still starts without a heading of the section's level, the gate puts back the original heading and the blank lines after it before rendering; otherwise applying the edit would delete the heading from the doc.

## Two comment variants

- **Suggestion.** Used only when the whole section, trailing blank lines included, lies inside one head-side hunk of that doc in the PR diff. GitHub only accepts review comments on diff lines, so this is the one case where the comment can sit on the doc's own lines. It is a GitHub `suggestion` block replacing exactly those lines, with the reason and no checkbox. The suggestion restates the section's trailing blank lines, otherwise applying it would eat the gap before the next heading. The code fence is made longer than any backtick run in the content so proposed code fences cannot close it early.
- **Checkbox.** Used for everything else: the doc is not in the diff, the section only partly overlaps a hunk or spans two, or the doc is new. The comment sits on the proposal's anchor line (a changed code line) and holds the reason, the doc path and section, the edit as a `diff` block (old section lines `-`, new lines `+`; a new doc shows only added lines plus its index entry), and an "Apply this change" task-list item.

## Identity and re-runs

A proposal's identity is its doc path plus its normalized section heading (leading `#` and whitespace stripped; path alone for a new doc), hashed to a short ID. The gate remembers each proposal's ID, comment ID and URL, and state (`open`, `applied`, or `outdated`), plus the summary comment ID, per PR.

On each run, after the check run is created, the gate reconciles the new proposals against what it remembers:

- **Same proposal again:** its comment is edited in place. The PR's comment count does not change across pushes.
- **New proposal:** a new review comment.
- **Proposal gone:** its comment and summary row are marked `outdated`; the old body stays readable under an "Outdated" notice. The gate never deletes a comment: that would erase the thread's replies and history, and a proposal that returns would have to start over. A proposal that returns after being outdated reopens its old comment.
- **No impact:** every earlier proposal is marked outdated and the check is `success`.
- **Summary:** one issue comment listing every proposal with doc path, section, a link to its comment, and state. It is edited in place, and only created when there is something to list or one already exists.

A comment keeps its location and variant across edits. GitHub cannot move a review comment, and replacing it would churn the thread. A suggestion block on the wrong lines would overwrite them when applied, so on edit the suggestion body is used only if the existing comment already sits on that doc at the same lines; otherwise the body is the checkbox variant. If a user deletes a proposal's comment, an open proposal gets a fresh comment, and an outdated one is skipped rather than resurrected.

## Markers and crash recovery

Every proposal comment starts with a hidden `<!-- pollux-agent:proposal:ID -->` and the summary with `<!-- pollux-agent:summary -->`. The gate lists the PR's comments before writing and, when its stored state lacks a comment ID, adopts the comment carrying the marker. It adopts or edits only comments written by the App's own bot user, with the marker as the body's first line: anyone can paste a marker into a comment (proposal IDs are hashes of public data), and adopting theirs would make every later edit fail with 403. So if a run stops after GitHub accepted a comment but before the gate saved its ID, the next run reuses that comment instead of posting a second. Before its first create, a run saves the proposals it is about to post, so even a run that crashed on its very first post leaves state behind; the next run then lists comments and adopts or outdates them, including when it finds no impact. State is saved again after all writes succeed. The concluded state (check done, run cleared) is saved before comments are posted, so a comment failure cannot leave an armed run for the deadline sweep to overwrite a success with neutral. Any other failed run is redone by the next push or re-run (see [Job queue](job-queue.md)).

## Known limits

- If a later push deletes the anchor line, GitHub shows its own "Outdated" badge on a still-open proposal; the gate's state is unaffected.
- The two GitHub comment APIs (review and issue) have separate ID spaces and edit endpoints, so the gate tracks which kind each comment is.

proposals.content:
## Flow (phase 1 target)

1. A PR is opened or updated; GitHub sends `pull_request` to the backend.
2. The backend lists the PR's changed files; the analysis runner maps them to docs through each doc's `covers` globs on its own checkout of the head commit (see [0002](decisions/0002-docs-structure.md)).
3. The LLM compares the diff with those docs and returns "no impact" or proposed edits.
4. The backend sets the `pollux-agent` check: `success` for no impact, `action_required` otherwise, and posts one review comment per proposal plus a summary comment (see [Proposal output](features/proposal-output.md)).
4a. If analysis fails or the PR is over the size limits, the check ends neutral with a fixed cause and the summary offers a "Re-run analysis" checkbox; GitHub's Re-run on the check does the same. The check never stays pending.
5. A user with write access applies one proposal or all of them, which commits the edits to the PR branch and triggers a new analysis, or skips the check for one commit or the whole PR with a reason, which turns the check `success`. These actions come from checkboxes in the comments or `/pollux-agent` commands, arrive as `issue_comment` and `pull_request_review_comment` webhooks, and run as per-PR comment jobs (see [Proposal output](features/proposal-output.md)).

proposals.reason: The App now acts on review comment edits and on new and edited issue comments (Apply, Skip, commands), not just the Re-run tick.
proposals.content:
## Events

Subscribe to: Pull request, Pull request review comment (a ticked "Apply this change" box), Issue comment (new comments for `/pollux-agent` commands and skip reasons; edits for ticked Apply all, Skip, and Re-run analysis boxes on the summary comment), Check run (GitHub's Re-run on the `pollux-agent` check), Workflow run (tells the backend a dispatched analysis run finished). Apply and Skip are limited to senders with write access, which the backend checks through the API; no extra App permission is needed. The App adds reactions to the comments it acts on, using its Issues and Pull requests write permissions.

proposals.content:
---
title: Deploy
summary: Run pollux on a single host with Docker Compose, and how the auto-update timer deploys new commits of main.
covers:
  - Dockerfile
  - compose.yaml
  - .dockerignore
  - deploy/**
---

# Deploy

The production deploy is a single host running the backend with Docker Compose. Configure the GitHub App first (see [GitHub App](github-app.md) and [Setup](setup.md)).

## Image

The `Dockerfile` builds `cmd/server` and `cmd/healthcheck` as static binaries and copies them into a distroless `nonroot` image. The image has no shell or curl, so the health probe is the `healthcheck` binary, which GETs a URL and fails unless it answers 200. `.dockerignore` keeps everything but `backend/` out of the build context, so `.env`, `*.pem`, and database files never enter the image.

## Compose

`compose.yaml` runs one `pollux` service:

- The root file system is read-only with a tmpfs `/tmp`, all capabilities are dropped, and `no-new-privileges` is set.
- The port is published on `127.0.0.1:8080` only; put a reverse proxy in front of it for GitHub webhooks.
- Settings come from `.env`. `GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE` in `.env` is required: it is the host path of the app's private key, bind-mounted read-only at `/run/secrets/github-app.pem`. Compose overrides `DATABASE_PATH` (`/data/pollux.db`, on the `pollux-data` volume) and `ADDR` (`:8080`).
- The health check runs `/healthcheck http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz` every 30 seconds.

## Auto-update

`deploy/pollux-update.timer` runs `deploy/pollux-update.service` one minute after boot and every 2 minutes after that. The service runs `deploy/pollux-update.sh` from the checkout at `~/pollux-agent`, as a user unit.

The script fetches `origin/main` and does nothing when that commit is already deployed or already failed. Otherwise it switches the checkout to the commit and runs `docker compose up -d --build --wait`. On success it records the commit as deployed. On failure it records the commit as failed so the timer does not retry it, rolls back to the last deployed commit if there is one, and exits non-zero. The next merge to `main` clears the failure. State lives in `$XDG_STATE_HOME/pollux` (default `~/.local/state/pollux`), and a lock stops overlapping runs.

facts.fact: pollux runs as one Docker Compose container on a single host, published on 127.0.0.1:8080 only, with Tailscale Funnel on the host forwarding public HTTPS to it.
The SQLite database lives in the named volume pollux-data; docker compose down -v deletes it along with the queue and PR state.
The container runs as uid 65532 on a distroless image with no shell, so the GitHub App private key file must be readable by that uid.
A systemd user timer polls origin/main every 2 minutes, deploys a new commit with docker compose up --build --wait, and redeploys the last good commit if the build or health check fails.

proposals.content:
## Flow

1. A push to a PR reaches the gate. It dispatches the workflow on the **default branch**, passing the head SHA, PR number, and a fresh nonce. Dispatching the default branch's copy means a PR cannot change the workflow, its tools, or its secrets.
2. GitHub returns the run ID. The gate stores the run ID, nonce, head SHA, and a deadline on the PR's state and puts the check in progress.
3. The workflow checks out the head commit and runs Claude Code, then uploads a result artifact (always, even on failure).
4. A `workflow_run` completed event arrives. The run ID maps to its PR.
5. The runner downloads the artifact. The gate accepts it only if the run is the one dispatched for the PR's current head and the artifact's head SHA and nonce match.
6. Proposals outside `docs/` or not matching the schema are rejected, as is a result with no proposals and an empty or blank `no_impact_reason`. Otherwise the same transition as the server runner concludes the check: success ("No doc impact" with a reason) or action_required with the proposals.

proposals.reason: Branch handling changed: an existing branch with a PR is no longer force-reset; a bot's PR is adopted and a human's fails the attempt.
proposals.content:
## Opening the PR

The branch `pollux-agent/docs-scaffold` is created off the default tip, with one commit and one PR into the default branch. If the branch already exists at another commit, pollux first looks for a pull request opened from it, because resetting the branch would close that PR. A PR opened by a bot (the App) is adopted as the scaffold PR, with no reset, commit, or new PR. A PR opened by a human fails the attempt, and the error names it. Only a branch with no PR is force-reset to the default tip before committing, so pollux never opens a PR from content it did not commit. When several PRs exist from the branch, an open one is preferred over closed ones. The validated files are stored as soon as they are written, so a failed commit or PR step retries without running the model again. A crash after the branch or PR exists is recovered by adopting them, not creating duplicates. If creating the PR fails and the PR found afterwards was not opened by a bot, the attempt fails rather than adopting it.

Any failure before the PR exists, including a workflow run that fails, is cancelled, or passes its deadline, leaves the repo's state retryable. Waiting checks then say an attempt failed, and the next PR event on a docs-less PR tries again. After 3 failed attempts the scaffold stops for good and the checks say it could not be written, so `docs/` has to be added by hand.

facts.fact: Before resetting the pollux-agent/docs-scaffold branch, pollux looks up a pull request opened from it.
A pull request from the branch opened by a bot is adopted instead of resetting the branch, so no second scaffold PR is opened.
A pull request from the branch by anyone else fails the attempt without changing the branch; the branch is force-reset only when no pull request exists from it.
